clue.text: Wine with no lack of body?

definitions.note: a cryptic description, not a synonym: places full of bodies

blocks.note: first meaning: a Bordeaux wine region and its wine
second meaning: burial plots, which are never short of a corpse

explanation.surface: A wine buff praises a full-bodied red.
explanation.walkthrough: Body in wine talk means fullness of flavour; read literally, a place with no lack of bodies is a burial site. GRAVES is a red and white wine from near Bordeaux.
explanation.definitionFit: Graves is a district of Bordeaux whose name labels its wines, and graves in a cemetery each hold a corpse.

clue.text: Allowed to get in the way in game

indicators.note: getting in means going inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a way is a road or course
let means permitted

explanation.surface: Someone is permitted to obstruct play in a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Roulette is a casino game of chance played with a spinning wheel and a ball.

clue.text: It's maximized by travelling light

blocks.note: surface reading: packing little luggage makes a journey easier
setter's reading: light itself in motion, the fastest thing in the universe

explanation.walkthrough: Travelling light is an idiom for carrying little baggage, but here it is light that travels, at the universe's top speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Speed in a given direction is greatest for light, whose rate in vacuum is the cosmic limit.

clue.text: Missionary in capital of state

blocks.note: first meaning: the apostle who carried the gospel to the Gentiles
second meaning: the seat of government of Minnesota

explanation.surface: A preacher working in a state's chief city.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostle made famous journeys spreading Christianity, and his name is borne by Minnesota's seat of government.

clue.text: Submarine may be made as usual with tin

indicators.note: something that may be made from raw material is built anew, so the letters get reassembled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Boat builders say a submarine can be made from tin, as normal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as usual' looks like one phrase, but 'as' only joins; the fodder is 'usual' plus 'tin'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nautilus is the famous submarine of Jules Verne's Captain Nemo, and the first nuclear-powered US Navy boat.

clue.text: Collection of native gods here

blocks.note: a national is a native of a country
the gods is the highest balcony in a theatre

explanation.surface: A display of indigenous deities is housed in this place.
explanation.walkthrough: The gods looks like deities; in British theatres it is the cheap upper gallery, high up near the ceiling.
explanation.definitionFit: London's National Gallery houses the nation's collection of paintings, so the building stands for the art it holds.

clue.text: Term in Irish college

blocks.note: first meaning: the summer term at Oxford and some other universities
second meaning: the college of the University of Dublin

explanation.surface: A semester spent at a university in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford's three terms are Michaelmas, Hilary and Trinity.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxford's summer teaching period bears this name, as does Dublin's ancient university college founded by Elizabeth I.

clue.text: She saw wartime service in the field

definitions.text: She saw wartime service in the field

blocks.note: surface reading: on the front line, in a combat zone
setter's reading: literally in a farm meadow, working the soil

explanation.walkthrough: In the field suggests battle; the Women's Land Army sent young women to work on British farms during the world wars.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Women's Land Army replaced male farmworkers away fighting, doing agricultural labour on the home front.

clue.text: Behaves like gulls or other birds

blocks.note: first meaning: a gull is a dupe, who believes whatever he is told
second meaning: fork-tailed summer migrants

explanation.surface: Seabird behaviour compared with that of different birds.
explanation.walkthrough: Gulls look like seabirds; a gull is also a gullible person, one who accepts a tall story without question.
explanation.definitionFit: Easily fooled people accept lies uncritically, and the swift-flying migrant passerines share the name.

clue.text: Second employer

blocks.note: surface reading: the boss someone works for next, or a firm ranked second
setter's reading: a second is the assistant at a pistol or sword fight, engaged by a combatant

explanation.walkthrough: Second looks like a number; it is the noun for the friend who attends a fighter in a formal fight of honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Each party to a formal fight of honour appoints a second to arrange matters, so the fighter is that helper's employer.

clue.text: Queen is given back colour

indicators.note: something given back travels in the opposite direction, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: Queen Anne, British monarch 1702-1714
taken as written

explanation.surface: A queen receives a colour, perhaps as a returned gift.
explanation.definitionFit: Sienna is an earth pigment, a yellowish or reddish brown named after the Tuscan city.

clue.text: Rout mice, dreadfully slain by King of Cats

indicators.note: done dreadfully means done badly and out of order, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Mice are scattered, then cruelly killed by the top cat.
explanation.walkthrough: In Romeo and Juliet, Mercutio mocks Tybalt as 'King of Cats' and is then killed by him.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Mercutio, Romeo's friend, dies from Tybalt's sword, the man he had nicknamed the prince of felines.

clue.text: Caveman last seen round the middle of Belgium

indicators.note: going round something encloses it, so one piece wraps the other
the middle of a word is its central letter, the only one kept here

blocks.note: the last one seen is the final one
the fourth of seven letters

explanation.surface: A prehistoric man was last spotted somewhere in central Belgium.
explanation.walkthrough: Caveman is not a troglodyte: FINGAL is the legendary hero who gives his name to Fingal's Cave on Staffa in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Fingal's Cave, the sea cave in the Hebrides, is named after the Gaelic giant-hero, so he is the man of the cave.

clue.text: Reckless type needing rent, not at home

blocks.note: a rent is a rip in cloth
someone not at home is out

explanation.surface: An irresponsible youth is short of rent money and never at his place.
explanation.walkthrough: Rent looks like money for housing; here it is a rip, the noun from rend.
explanation.definitionFit: A tearaway is an impetuous, unruly young person, a wild and heedless sort.

clue.text: Writer shares out parts

indicators.note: parts as a verb means separates, so the letters come apart and regroup

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An author distributes sections of her work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shares out' looks like the verb with parts as its object; parts is the verb and shares out the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Authoress is an old-fashioned word for a female novelist or poet.

clue.text: It's used to intensify a sort of light

definitions.note: describes the word rather than standing in for it

blocks.note: first meaning: the commonest adverb that boosts an adjective
second meaning: a coloured flare fired from a pistol as a signal

explanation.surface: Something makes a lamp shine brighter.
explanation.walkthrough: A Very light is a signal flare named after its American inventor, Edward Very.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb strengthens words such as good or bad, and Very lights are pistol-fired distress flares.

clue.text: It's this sort of drink

blocks.note: surface reading: a vague pointer to some unspecified beverage
setter's reading: 'It' is the bar abbreviation for Italian, as in gin and it

explanation.walkthrough: In a gin and it, 'it' stands for Italian, a sweet red fortified wine flavoured with herbs; so It is this kind of drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The aromatised fortified wine from Italy is abbreviated It in the cocktail gin and it.

clue.text: Critic who doesn't rely on first appearances?

definitions.text: Critic who doesn't rely on first appearances?

blocks.note: surface reading: a fair judge who looks below the surface
setter's reading: one who sees a show again, not only the first time

explanation.walkthrough: Split as re-view-er, the word means someone who views something a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre or book critic writes notices, and the word itself suggests a person who looks at things more than once.

clue.text: Brief state of regret thus expressed

indicators.note: made brief, a word is cut short and loses its ending

blocks.note: the largest US state

explanation.surface: A short-lived feeling of sorrow put into words.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the last two letters of the state gives ALAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Alas is an interjection uttered to show sorrow or disappointment, a sigh in word form.

clue.text: Recommend someone to deal with brief assignments

definitions.text: someone to deal with brief assignments

blocks.note: first meaning: speak in favour of a course

blocks.clueFragment: someone to deal with brief assignments
blocks.note: second meaning: a lawyer who takes on a brief, a case to argue

explanation.surface: Suggesting a person to handle short jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: Brief looks like short; in law a brief is the instructions for a barrister's case. In Scotland an advocate is a barrister.
explanation.definitionFit: To advocate is to urge or support a course, and an advocate is the courtroom pleader handed a case.

clue.text: Special radio set for space-traveller

indicators.note: something special is made to order, so the letters are rearranged into a new form

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A custom wireless built for an astronaut.
explanation.walkthrough: Space-traveller suggests an astronaut, but it is a rocky body orbiting the Sun.
explanation.definitionFit: An asteroid is a minor planet, a lump of rock moving through the solar system on its own orbit.

clue.text: Christian's enemy Edward frustrated

blocks.note: Captain Bligh of the Bounty, against whom Fletcher Christian led the mutiny
Ted is a familiar form of Edward

explanation.surface: A believer's foe called Edward was thwarted.
explanation.walkthrough: Christian looks like a believer, perhaps the hero of Pilgrim's Progress; it is Fletcher Christian, leader of the 1789 mutiny on HMS Bounty.
explanation.definitionFit: Blighted hopes are spoiled or ruined ones, so the word works for plans that are thwarted.

clue.text: Produce equals sign

blocks.note: first meaning: make two sides even, as with accounts
second meaning: the zodiac sign Libra, the scales

explanation.surface: Make an equals sign, as in arithmetic.
explanation.walkthrough: Equals sign looks like the symbol =; the clue splits after equals, and the sign is one of the zodiac.
explanation.definitionFit: Balancing accounts makes debits match credits, and Libra, the seventh zodiac constellation, is pictured as a pair of scales.

clue.text: Courageous about one, for the most part

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: manly as brave, in an old-fashioned sense
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Being brave about just one thing, generally.
explanation.definitionFit: Mainly means chiefly or largely, which is the sense of the phrase about the greater portion.

clue.text: Inspect what drivers of hansoms do

definitions.note: describes an action, a verb phrase like the answer

blocks.note: first meaning: examine something quickly
second meaning: the cabman sits high at the back and sees over the roof

explanation.surface: Check how Victorian cab drivers went about their work.
explanation.walkthrough: A hansom is a two-wheeled horse cab whose driver sat on a raised seat behind the passengers, peering above them.
explanation.definitionFit: To look over a document is to examine it, and a hansom cabby perched aloft literally gazes past the hood.

clue.text: Take turns off to relax

blocks.note: first meaning: uncoil a spool or reel
second meaning: calm down after stress

explanation.surface: Taking breaks in shifts so everyone can rest.
explanation.walkthrough: Take turns looks like sharing a rota; the turns are coils of thread or cable.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwinding a reel removes its coils, and figuratively a person unwinds when tension eases away.

clue.text: Aircraft controller's alternative to flights in US

blocks.note: first meaning: the hinged tail surface that makes a plane climb or dive
second meaning: the American word for a lift, used instead of stairs

explanation.surface: An air traffic controller suggests another way to travel than flying in America.
explanation.walkthrough: Flights look like air journeys; they are flights of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: The tailplane flap governing pitch is so named, and Americans call a lift by this term.

clue.text: Disturber of flesh or backside of pony

definitions.text: Disturber of flesh or backside of pony

indicators.note: whatever is disturbed is thrown out of order, so the letters following get mixed
the backside of a word is its tail, so only its final letter counts

blocks.note: taken as written
the final letter

explanation.surface: Something that pesters the skin or rump of a pony.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: a horsefly bites horses' flesh and rumps.
explanation.definitionFit: Horseflies are biting insects that torment livestock, piercing skin to drink blood.

clue.text: Boyfriend about to start running?

definitions.note: describes the word's place in a starter's call, not a synonym

blocks.note: first meaning: a regular sweetheart
second meaning: the word said just before 'go' at the start of a race

explanation.surface: A girl's partner is on the point of taking up jogging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready, steady, go!' is the British call to start a race; steady comes just before the off.
explanation.definitionFit: A steady is a regular partner in courtship, and the second word of the race-start call comes just before setting off.
